steps.note: Create a test event for the counter-offer flow.
Ensure the RFQ exposes the counter-offer action required by the case.
Use an RFQ stage because the case requires the RFQ counter-offer option.
Give the event a searchable title and satisfy the create flow requirement.
Apply the first available RFQ template.
Add a line item so the RFQ has a bid sheet.
Populate the RFQ pricing sheet before publishing.
Commit a valid bidding schedule.
Invite one QA vendor who can submit and answer the counter offer.
Publish the test RFQ.
Confirm the event reached a real published project page.
Confirm the vendor bid was accepted.
Open the buyer comparison view containing the vendor bid.
Send the buyer's counter offer to the vendor.
Confirm the buyer grid records that the counter offer was initiated.
Have the vendor answer by accepting the pending counter offer.
Return to the buyer portal to inspect the buyer-side activity history.
Confirm the buyer view records the vendor's acceptance before checking activity.
Open the RFQ stage's Order Activity drawer.
Confirm the Order Activity drawer opened.
Check that the activity history contains a counter-offer entry.
Check that the displayed activity reflects the answered or accepted counter offer.
